rationales.quote: You seem to be like all that!
rationales.explanation: Jillian expresses an initially positive impression of the founder while asking about her background.

rationales.quote: Talk about how do you qualify the participants, how do you onboard the participants.
rationales.explanation: Jillian probes the operational process for qualifying and onboarding participants.

rationales.quote: And who are your customers now?
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks for evidence of current customer adoption.

rationales.quote: Okay. And what are your revenues?
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks about revenue performance as part of assessing the business model.

rationales.quote: So have you looked at your payment model? Assessed it? Re-assessed it?
rationales.explanation: Jillian directly probes whether the monetization model has been evaluated and refined.

rationales.quote: And the yearly contract is…
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks for the value of the annual contract to understand the monetization model.

rationales.quote: How much have you raised?
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks how much capital the company has already attracted.

rationales.quote: Are you looking at markets outside of Africa?
rationales.explanation: Jillian probes the geographic scope of the addressable market.

rationales.quote: This is when you drop the mic.
rationales.explanation: Jillian reacts enthusiastically to the founder's preceding case for the African market opportunity.

rationales.quote: I've actually invested in six companies in Africa. Okay. Five went belly up.
rationales.explanation: Jillian cites multiple failed African investments as relevant prior experience shaping her hesitation.

rationales.quote: I am worried because I have scars because I have invested in Africa and just didn't know what the hell I was doing.
rationales.explanation: Jillian explicitly attributes her concern to negative prior investment experience in Africa.

rationales.quote: But I got burned.
rationales.explanation: Jillian invokes prior investment losses as a reason against proceeding.

rationales.quote: Five times.
rationales.explanation: Jillian clarifies the extent of her prior losses, reinforcing the experience-based objection.

rationales.quote: I think it’s my scar tissue.
rationales.explanation: Jillian explicitly explains her refusal as being driven by scars from past investments.

rationales.quote: I also don't think I can add the value that some of these other funds we're going to make introductions to, who have boots on the ground.
rationales.explanation: Jillian believes locally embedded funds can contribute more value than she can.

rationales.quote: what can I add here?
rationales.explanation: Jillian reiterates uncertainty about the value she could contribute to the company.

rationales.quote: Maybe she hasn't gone - has she pitched to -
rationales.explanation: During the immediate investor debrief, Jillian asks whether the founder has sought local-fund participation.

rationales.quote: It's not defensible.
rationales.explanation: Jillian states that the company lacks a defensible competitive advantage.

Use ONLY the supplied taxonomy labels and their definitions. Do not predict what the VC should think, infer unspoken motives,
borrow another investor's reasoning, or turn a founder claim into the target's belief. Do not force every taxonomy label.
Extract material questions, concerns, supporting arguments and explicit investment-decision explanations. A neutral factual
question is queried/neutral, not a negative belief. Greetings, jokes, biography, simple confirmations and bare In/Out without
a reason are not rationales. Distinguish closely related taxonomy definitions; do not add broad redundant labels.
Retain each distinct rationale-bearing target utterance and exact evidence turn. Multiple labels on a turn are allowed only
when distinct concepts are expressed. For a repeated concept in different substantive turns retain each occurrence.
Quotes must be exact nonempty substrings of that turn's attributed_text, never continuation narration or another speaker.
The full text is included for context, but only attributed_text is eligible quote evidence.
Classify timing: original_pitch includes Q&A AND the entire original in-room decision discussion; later_commentary includes
post-pitch interviews, later diligence and subsequent updates; teaser is an opening preview/repeated future clip. Use unclear
when timing is uncertain. Do not use the redacted input cutoff as the end of original in-room discussion. Same-session
reversals stay original_pitch. Immediate investor-only debrief in the same room after the founder exits also stays
original_pitch; it is NOT later_commentary. Reserve later_commentary for separate interviews, diligence or updates. Do not mix retrospective opinions into original-pitch scoring.
Direction is positive/negative/neutral towards investing in this company. Salience primary means a stated major reason, not
merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.

rationales.quote: You seem to be like all that!
rationales.explanation: Jillian expresses a favorable initial impression of Mariam's overall capabilities.

rationales.quote: Talk about how do you qualify the participants, how do you onboard the participants.
rationales.explanation: Jillian probes whether the participant qualification and onboarding process is operationally workable.

rationales.quote: And who are your customers now?
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks for evidence of current customer adoption.

rationales.quote: So have you looked at your payment model? Assessed it? Re-assessed it?
rationales.explanation: Jillian directly examines whether the company's monetization model has been tested and refined.

rationales.quote: And the yearly contract is…
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks for the annual contract value to understand the company's monetization.

rationales.quote: How much have you raised?
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks how much investor capital the company has already attracted.

rationales.quote: Are you looking at markets outside of Africa?
rationales.explanation: Jillian probes whether the company's addressable geographic market extends beyond Africa.

rationales.quote: This is when you drop the mic.
rationales.explanation: Jillian enthusiastically endorses Mariam's preceding case for the size and growth of the African market.

rationales.quote: You're good.
rationales.explanation: Jillian positively assesses Mariam's persuasive performance in the pitch discussion.

rationales.quote: I've actually invested in six companies in Africa. Okay. Five went belly up.
rationales.explanation: Jillian cites the failure of five prior African investments as the reason she is torn about investing.

rationales.quote: I am worried because I have scars because I have invested in Africa
rationales.explanation: Jillian explicitly says that scars from her prior African investments are causing concern.

rationales.quote: just didn't know what the hell I was doing. Right. So I have no idea.
rationales.explanation: Jillian acknowledges that she lacks the relevant knowledge to assess and navigate African investments confidently.

rationales.quote: But I got burned.
rationales.explanation: In response to encouragement to invest, Jillian invokes her prior losses as an argument against doing so.

rationales.quote: Five times.
rationales.explanation: Jillian emphasizes the number of prior losses to reinforce her experience-based refusal.

rationales.quote: I'm out. Okay. But what I can do is I can introduce you to four funds that invest in Africa. And I wish I could. I think it’s my scar tissue.
rationales.explanation: Jillian explicitly attributes her decision not to invest to scar tissue from her previous African investments.

rationales.quote: I also don't think I can add the value that some of these other funds we're going to make introductions to, who have boots on the ground.
rationales.explanation: Jillian explains that locally embedded funds could provide more useful support than she could.

rationales.quote: what can I add here?
rationales.explanation: Jillian rhetorically reiterates her concern that she cannot contribute sufficient value to the company.

rationales.quote: Maybe she hasn't gone - has she pitched to -
rationales.explanation: In the immediate debrief, Jillian asks whether the founder has approached local investors, probing the significance of their absence from the round.

rationales.quote: It's not defensible.
rationales.explanation: Jillian concludes that the product or technology lacks defensibility against competitors.

Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.

rationales.quote: You seem to be like all that!
rationales.explanation: Jillian expresses a favorable initial impression of Mariam's overall capabilities.

rationales.quote: Talk about how do you qualify the participants, how do you onboard the participants.
rationales.explanation: Jillian probes whether the participant qualification and onboarding process is operationally workable.

rationales.quote: And who are your customers now?
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks for evidence of current customer adoption.

rationales.quote: So have you looked at your payment model? Assessed it? Re-assessed it?
rationales.explanation: Jillian directly examines whether the company's monetization model has been tested and refined.

rationales.quote: And the yearly contract is…
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks for the annual contract value to understand the company's monetization.

rationales.quote: How much have you raised?
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks how much investor capital the company has already attracted.

rationales.quote: Are you looking at markets outside of Africa?
rationales.explanation: Jillian probes whether the company's addressable geographic market extends beyond Africa.

rationales.quote: This is when you drop the mic.
rationales.explanation: Jillian enthusiastically endorses Mariam's preceding case for the size and growth of the African market.

rationales.quote: You're good.
rationales.explanation: Jillian positively assesses Mariam's persuasive performance in the pitch discussion.

rationales.quote: I've actually invested in six companies in Africa. Okay. Five went belly up.
rationales.explanation: Jillian cites the failure of five prior African investments as the reason she is torn about investing.

rationales.quote: I am worried because I have scars because I have invested in Africa
rationales.explanation: Jillian explicitly says that scars from her prior African investments are causing concern.

rationales.quote: just didn't know what the hell I was doing. Right. So I have no idea.
rationales.explanation: Jillian acknowledges that she lacks the relevant knowledge to assess and navigate African investments confidently.

rationales.quote: But I got burned.
rationales.explanation: In response to encouragement to invest, Jillian invokes her prior losses as an argument against doing so.

rationales.quote: Five times.
rationales.explanation: Jillian emphasizes the number of prior losses to reinforce her experience-based refusal.

rationales.quote: I'm out. Okay. But what I can do is I can introduce you to four funds that invest in Africa. And I wish I could. I think it’s my scar tissue.
rationales.explanation: Jillian explicitly attributes her decision not to invest to scar tissue from her previous African investments.

rationales.quote: I also don't think I can add the value that some of these other funds we're going to make introductions to, who have boots on the ground.
rationales.explanation: Jillian explains that locally embedded funds could provide more useful support than she could.

rationales.quote: what can I add here?
rationales.explanation: Jillian rhetorically reiterates her concern that she cannot contribute sufficient value to the company.

rationales.quote: Maybe she hasn't gone - has she pitched to -
rationales.explanation: In the immediate debrief, Jillian asks whether the founder has approached local investors, probing the significance of their absence from the round.

rationales.quote: It's not defensible.
rationales.explanation: Jillian concludes that the product or technology lacks defensibility against competitors.
